sections.h2: Hardwood, not bagasse, is the largest of TNPL's three pulping lines

chart.title: Hardwood pulping at 730 tonnes a day exceeds bagasse's 550
chart.sub: TNPL Karur pulping lines as of 31 March 2025, tonnes per day.
chart.source: CARE Ratings press release on TNPL.

sections.means: Bagasse is a real but second-largest line at Karur, with hardwood carrying more tonnes.
sections.todo: Recheck the claim that bagasse is TNPL's primary furnish against the 730 tonnes a day of hardwood.

sections.h2: Agro-residue is the smallest fibre stream in India's paper industry

chart.title: Recycled fibre supplies 74-76% of the industry; agro-residue 6-8%
chart.sub: Industry fibre mix as published by the Indian Paper Manufacturers Association.
chart.source: IPMA, overview page on its website.

sections.means: Agro-residue is not a growing share of national fibre, and the trade body's public asks do not name it.
sections.todo: Search IPMA's own press archive for any bagasse capacity ask before treating it as an industry priority.

sections.h2: Domestic wood supply falls short of the paper industry's demand

chart.title: Wood demand of around 11 million tonnes a year exceeds the 9 million supplied
chart.sub: Annual wood for paper, million tonnes, as cited by IPMA's president.
chart.source: Business Standard, coverage of IPMA statements.

sections.means: The wood gap, which the post projects toward 15 million tonnes, is the supply problem IPMA publicly names.
sections.todo: Track the projected widening of the wood gap before treating bagasse as a substitute for pulpwood.
